findings.before: Required custom checkpoint/state restoration during assignment had no explicit recovery/readiness rule. Existing ownership epochs and completed-offset tracking covered processing after initialization.
findings.consequence: An exception during custom initialization followed by a successful callback with no newly added partitions can leave an owned partition unrestored; continuing can use an unintended checkpoint and process or commit beyond required work.
findings.correction: Conditionally separate readiness from membership for custom restoration, preserve pending initialization per partition/epoch, and require bounded explicit restore/seek recovery or consumer recreation before dispatch/commit.
findings.evidence: Kafka 4.1.0 ConsumerCoordinator lines 392–419/461–470; AbstractCoordinator lines 506–516; AbstractMembershipManager lines 859–866/1194–1217.
findings.classification: Supported decision gap; source-backed mechanism, not a measured behavioral defect in a user application.

findings.correction: Added fault-injection coverage for partial initialization, later empty callbacks, recovery position, and late old-epoch restoration; distinguishes application guard mocks from actual client/protocol behavior.
findings.consequence: A happy rebalance test can otherwise miss dispatch/commit from a partition whose required initialization never completed.

findings.location: External source discrepancy; preserved under isolated artifacts
findings.detail: The Kafka 4.1.2 listener Javadoc broadly says callback exceptions do not cause retries. Tagged 4.1.0 classic onJoinComplete and consumer-protocol reconciliation paths contain retry/re-entry behavior and potentially empty added-partition sets. The skill therefore makes no universal callback retry/non-retry promise and pins its example to 4.1.0.
findings.status: Recorded; no unverified universal claim added.
